title: Start and stop the workflow runtime with the Hermes gateway lifecycle
description: Audit found register(ctx) only registers tools and slash commands; get_runtime() starts the supervisor lazily on first tool/API access. A fresh gateway can therefore leave cron schedules and interrupted-run recovery idle until someone invokes the plugin. Wire supported Hermes startup/shutdown or auxiliary-task lifecycle without eager provider calls; reconcile schedules and recover expired leases at startup, dispose workers on unload, and verify cold-restart behavior without an initial tool request.
notes: Implemented in 1.0.1: registration starts per-home runtimes before any tool/API call; startup reconciles cron files and recovers expired leases; ctx.on_unload owns cleanup, with atexit fallback; ContextVars propagate into the supervisor and handlers stay bound to their registration home. Agent workers skip supervisor startup. Reference-counted, idempotent ownership shares a runtime with FastAPI/ASGI lifespan without stopping a plugin-owned runtime on HTTP shutdown. Tests cover cold boot, due schedules, recovery, unload cancellation/lease release, reload generations, profile isolation, and shared HTTP ownership. Verified with the real installed Hermes PluginContext/ledger: all tools register and unload removes tools/stops runtime. Full test environment: 36 tests pass; native Python 3.14: 34 pass/2 optional dependency skips; lint/format pass.
close_reason: Automatic startup, schedule reconciliation, recovery and owned shutdown implemented and verified
